layers.process: You need your passport to travel between Peninsular Malaysia and Sabah, even though the trip stays inside Malaysia. East Malaysia (Sabah and Sarawak) has its own entry checks.

layers.authority: Malaysian security authorities and police in the Eastern Sabah Security Zone (ESSZone); the Sabah Government restricts use of the waterways
layers.process: A 6 pm to 6 am curfew on water travel applies in 6 coastal districts of eastern Sabah, including waters up to 3 nautical miles (5.5 km) offshore. In daylight, vessels in the waters off Lahad Datu and Sandakan need a permit or permission from police, and all vessels must keep to designated routes. Resort-run water activities at night, including diving and fishing, are banned. Authorities may extend the curfew each fortnight; travelling by water in curfew hours without permission can bring a fine or up to 6 months' jail. The ESSZone covers Beluran, Kinabatangan, Kota Marudu, Kudat, Kunak, Lahad Datu, Pitas, Sandakan, Semporna and Tawau.

Sipadan Island Park, international visitors: conservation fee RM100 a person (about A$35.05) and scuba diving fee RM350 (A$122.68). The page says fees can vary by activity and visitor type. A$ at RBA 30 Oct 2026: A$1 = MYR 2.853.

Diving at Sipadan runs on booked permits. Sabah Parks decides permit issue and availability. Registered dive operators can book up to six months ahead at the Sabah Parks head office in Kota Kinabalu or the park office in Semporna, with a 50% deposit, one booking list per dive date, and full payment two weeks before. Cancelling more than two weeks before keeps 10% of the fees; cancelling later forfeits everything paid. No accommodation has been allowed on the island since it became a marine park in 2004. The page gives no daily cap.

Tunku Abdul Rahman Park (off Kota Kinabalu), non-Malaysian entrance per person per day: RM25 for 18 and over (about A$8.76), RM20 for 17 and under or 60 and over (A$7.01). Kuraman scuba diving fee RM200 for international visitors (A$70.10), which the page marks as needing confirmation with the park. A$ at RBA 30 Oct 2026: A$1 = MYR 2.853.

zone-requirements.note: Sabah and Sarawak keep their own immigration powers under Part VII of Malaysia's Immigration Act 1959/63 (the Act wasn't read on an official page).

laws.rule: Sabah and Sarawak keep their own immigration control under the Immigration Act 1959/63: travelling between the Peninsula, Sabah and Sarawak needs a valid passport (no visa), and you clear immigration again on arrival.

Climbing Mount Kinabalu needs a booked package from Sabah Parks (online only; accommodation, permit and insurance are paid at booking). Every climber goes with a park mountain guide: one guide for up to five climbers, RM350 paid in cash. Names can't be changed after booking and cancellations are non-refundable. As at 19 September 2026, bookings for the 2027 season had not opened. 2026 rates for international adults: permit RM400 (RM200 for 17 and under) and a conservation fee of RM50 (RM25), with guide and transport extra. Not converted to AUD here (no dated rate held).
laws.penalty_signal: Sabah Parks shared a news report (The Star, September 2026) of a foreign climber fined RM25,000 for illegal entry into Mount Kinabalu. The fine is from a news report, so treat it as a signal.

laws.rule: Sipadan Island Park: diving needs a permit booked through Sabah Parks (usually by a registered dive operator), and Sabah Parks makes the final decision on availability. International conservation fee RM100 and scuba fee RM350 a person (about A$35.05 and A$122.68; RBA 30 Oct 2026, A$1 = MYR 2.853).

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Dress modestly, especially at places of worship. Remove shoes before entering mosques and homes. Don't point with your index finger. A handshake is generally fine. At Kota Kinabalu City Mosque all visitors must register, wear the coverall provided (rental RM 5 to RM 10, about A$1.75 to about A$3.51 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026), bring no food or drink and not pose inappropriately in photos.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: At the City Mosque, observe off-limit areas and don't imitate prayer. Entry RM 5; closed Fridays.
